passage: Monday: On the school bus, two older girls took Bidisha's hair clips and tossed them over her head. Nazia's mouth went dry. If she spoke, she thought, they would start on her next. She said nothing and watched the traffic. Wednesday: She wrote a short note without her name and dropped it into the teacher's box. Her hand shook. Friday: At the bus stop, Nazia sat down next to Bidisha and offered her a peppermint. "Those girls were awful," she said softly. Bidisha nodded. The teacher had begun sitting on the bus each morning, and nobody asked who had written the note.

qa.q: How did Nazia let the teacher know without giving her name?
qa.a: She wrote a short note without her name and dropped it into the teacher's box.

qa.q: Why did Nazia stay silent on Monday?
qa.a: She was afraid that if she spoke up, the older girls would start on her next.

qa.q: What safe choices did Nazia find when she was too scared to confront the girls?
qa.a: She reported it anonymously with a note, and then she was kind to Bidisha afterwards.

qa.q: How might Bidisha have felt when Nazia sat beside her and offered a peppermint?
qa.a: Bidisha probably felt comforted and less alone, since someone had noticed and spoke kindly, and she nodded in agreement.

grounding: A frightened bystander reports quietly and is kind to the target afterwards, over several days.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Wednesday.
Akash came to my room during the last period, very quiet. He said that on Monday, two Class 7 boys trapped Tushar in the washroom and took his lunch money. Akash had been there but said nothing.
"If I'd spoken, they'd have come for me next," he said. His hands were twisting in his lap.
I told him his fear made sense and that telling me later still counted. He asked if his name could stay out of it. I said yes.
He said he'd also sat with Tushar at lunch today. I spoke to the Class 7 teacher before the end of the day.

qa.q: Where did the Class 7 boys trap Tushar?
What was Akash afraid of on Monday?
qa.a: He was afraid that if he spoke up, the Class 7 boys would target him next.

qa.q: What safe choices did Akash make after Monday?
qa.a: He told the counsellor later, asked for his name to be kept private, and was kind to Tushar by sitting with him at lunch.

qa.q: How might Tushar feel when Akash sits with him at lunch?
qa.a: Tushar may feel less alone after what happened in the washroom, even without knowing Akash reported it.

grounding: A boy who stayed silent out of fear later tells a counsellor privately and is kind to the target, showing safe ways to act.

passage:
Thursday
Today at break two boys from 6C pushed Chaitanya against the tap and poured water down his shirt. I was right there. I wanted to shout STOP but my throat locked. If I did, they'd come for me next, I just know it.
I felt awful all through Science.
Then I remembered the worry box outside the staffroom. At lunch I wrote on a slip: "6C boys wet Chaitanya at the tap at break." No name. I dropped it in.
By last period, Ma'am called the two boys out.
After school I walked out with Chaitanya and shared my biscuits. He didn't say much, but he smiled.
Lalremsiami

qa.q: What did the boys pour down Chaitanya's shirt?
Why did Lalremsiami's throat lock at the tap?
qa.a: Lalremsiami was scared of becoming the next target, and that fear stopped any words coming out.

qa.q: Which safe choices did Lalremsiami make?
qa.a: Lalremsiami used the worry box to report without a name, then walked out with Chaitanya and shared biscuits.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya feel when someone walks out with him after school?
qa.a: Chaitanya may feel comforted and less alone after a bad day, which is why he smiles.

grounding: A child too scared to speak up at the time reports anonymously and is kind to the target afterwards.
